blind_prior_baseline.derivation: wide_reset (scripts/collect_apple_wide.py L44-45, 91-93) places object_xy at centre (0.34, -0.18) plus uniform(-0.03, +0.03) independently per axis. The blind error is therefore the norm of a point uniform on a 6 cm x 6 cm square centred on zero; its median is 2.3937 cm (2e6 samples, and asserted in tests/test_policy_preflight.py).
blind_prior_baseline.independently_confirmed: Reproduced to the digit by the reviewer and by the coordinator.
blind_prior_baseline.standing_rule_is_necessary_not_sufficien: The rule 'every absolute pre-flight threshold must sit strictly below the blind prior' is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. It rules out a gate that a pure prior passes outright; it does not rule out a gate that a near-prior model passes. Only the ratio condition does that, and only the ratio condition is independent of the reset jitter width.
blind_prior_baseline.the_absolute_threshold_is_NOT_the_blind_: STATED EXPLICITLY so a future reader does not look at P3 = 2.0 cm against the 2.3937 cm prior, see a 0.39 cm gap, and conclude the gate is nearly toothless. The absolute thresholds are thin defences on their own. THE RATIO CONDITION IS WHAT CARRIES THE LOAD: a model that ignores the image produces the SAME output for a foreign frame as for the real one, so its shuffled-frame control error EQUALS its own error and its ratio is ~1.0. That fails <= 0.7 decisively, and by a margin that does not depend on the jitter width at all -- unlike the absolute thresholds, which do.
blind_prior_baseline.what_it_is: The median apple-position error of a predictor that always emits the reset centre and never reads the image.
blind_prior_baseline.why_it_is_recorded_here: So no future reader has to rediscover why the pre-flight gates sit where they do. Every absolute pre-flight threshold must sit STRICTLY BELOW this number or it certifies nothing. The first draft's P2 (2.5 cm) and P3 (3.0 cm) did not, and were tightened to 1.5 cm = 0.63x this baseline. Only 19.6% of resets land within 1.5 cm of the centre, which is why a 1.5 cm gate is not passable by a prior.

budget.why_n40_is_affordable: A feed-forward policy evaluates far more cheaply per command than the CEM ceiling: the G7 cap of 100 ms is already 6.2x under the ceiling's measured 0.621-0.649 s, and the expected cost (one encoder forward plus a 380k-parameter head) is another order below the cap. That is why n=40 is affordable where prior protocols could afford n=8.

C_frozen_gating.generator_cross_check_purpose: Re-running wide_reset and comparing to the stored values proves the stored cohort came from the COMMITTED RULE and not a lookalike. That purpose is fully served at 1e-12 m. Exact equality was the wrong assertion and CI caught it.
C_frozen_gating.one_ulp_platform_difference: IDENTIFIED, so the next person does not re-investigate. numpy's compiled Generator.uniform evaluates low + range * next_double; whether that multiply-add contracts to an FMA depends on the numpy build's compiler and target, so the result can differ by one ULP (~1.4e-17 m here) between macOS arm64 and Linux x86-64. The underlying PCG64 doubles are integer-derived and bit-exact everywhere; only the affine rescale differs. Reproduced locally: rng.uniform(-0.03, 0.03, 2) != [lo + (hi-lo)*x for x in raw] in the first element under numpy 2.5.3. Precedent: the wide corpus hit the same class of problem (scripts/collect_apple_wide.py plan hash; docs/experiments/apple_wide_collection_results_v1.md L174-179) and solved it with a platform-robust hash rounded to 1e-9 on every platform plus the exact hash on macOS arm64 only. This protocol needs no rounded hash because its digest is over stored decimals rather than recomputed floats.
C_frozen_gating.pin_check: regenerating seed 45200 from this rule reproduces benchmarks/manifests/apple-wide-grasp-closure-v3.json resets.45200 EXACTLY (object_xy [0.3229653854661023,-0.15092924454200007], plate_xy [0.5010270523751088,-0.1025915174158386]) Checked to a tolerance of 1e-12 m, not exact equality -- see generator_cross_check_tolerance.
C_frozen_gating.reset_rule: wide_reset (TASK-047): apple +-3 cm about (0.34,-0.18), plate +-2 cm about (0.49,-0.09)
C_frozen_gating.runner_must_clip_to_configured_bounds: BLOCKING requirement on scripts/evaluate_policy.py, alongside runner_must_reset_from_stored_values. ClonedPolicy.act clips to the CONTRACT range [-1, 1] because validate_actions demands it, but the protocol's frozen right-arm bounds are +-0.5. The runner must wire policy._check_pinned_bounds and clip emitted actions to the configured bounds, or a head could command twice the delta every prior generation operated under. Not yet wired: there is no closed-loop runner.
C_frozen_gating.runner_must_reset_from_stored_values: The evaluation runner MUST instantiate each reset from the stored object_xy/plate_xy in this manifest and MUST NOT recompute them from wide_reset at run time. Otherwise two machines could execute subtly different cohorts while both passing the digest check. This is a requirement on scripts/evaluate_policy.py, stated before it is written.
C_frozen_gating.tripwires_are_text_checks_and_must_be_up: BLOCKING requirement on scripts/evaluate_policy.py. The two constraints above are currently enforced by SOURCE-TEXT tripwires in tests/test_policy_preflight.py. A grep cannot prove the runner correct; it can only make the requirement impossible to miss at the moment the file is created, and nothing stronger is available now because you cannot import and introspect a file that does not exist. WHEN THAT FILE IS WRITTEN, THE TEXT CHECKS MUST BE REPLACED BY BEHAVIOURAL TESTS: (1) import the runner, hand it an action beyond the frozen +-0.5 right-arm bound, and assert that what actually reaches the embodiment is clipped to the bound; (2) assert that the resets the runner executes equal the stored manifest values rather than recomputed ones. Shipping the weak check plus this obligation is deliberate: a weak check that fires at the right moment beats a strong check that cannot be written, PROVIDED the debt is recorded rather than the weak check being treated as sufficient. NOTE on the bounds tripwire specifically: it is satisfied by a bare MENTION of lower_bounds/upper_bounds anywhere in the file, including in a comment or an unrelated config dump. It bites the case it was written for -- a runner authored with no awareness of the constraint -- but it is NOT a guarantee and must not be treated as one. The reset tripwire was upgraded from a text grep to an AST walk after a demonstrated false positive: it fired on a CORRECT runner whose docstring explained that it does not recompute from wide_reset. A tripwire that bites the person who got it right teaches people to weaken tripwires.
C_frozen_gating.what_freezes_the_cohort: THE STORED VALUES IN THIS MANIFEST ARE THE DEFINITION OF COHORT C, not the generator. cohort_sha256 is a sha256 over the stored decimals (json.dumps(resets, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'))). It never re-runs wide_reset, and json.loads -> float -> repr is idempotent because CPython's shortest-round-trip repr and correctly-rounded strtod are platform-independent. So the seal reproduces on ANY platform and is verifiable by a third party on a different machine.

R1_close_phase_starvation.derivation: 45 close commands (scripted.py phase budget) x 137 surviving train roots
R1_close_phase_starvation.pre_declared_reading: if G4 fails while G2 passes, the reading is close-phase data starvation, not 'cloning does not work', and Outcome C fires with a corpus spec that oversamples close
R1_close_phase_starvation.upper_bound_not_estimate: 45 close commands x 137 surviving train roots assumes every surviving root reaches and completes the close phase. Committed terminations are 115 success / 160 guard_refused / 65 policy_complete, so roots that stop early contribute fewer. The run records the exact count. The bound being an upper bound makes R1 worse, not better.
R1_close_phase_starvation.why_it_matters: Grasp-closure v3 proved the task is decided in the close phase and named the mechanism: LATERAL PALM DRIFT while the fingers shut. The v2 close cost is nearly flat in the lateral command, so over the eleven closing commands that command is statistically indistinguishable from the CEM's undirected proposal noise (mean |dxy| 0.219-0.313 against 0.228 for noise alone), the palm walks off the apple and the still-open thumb strikes it first (apple_wide_grasp_closure_v3.md L32-41). It is NOT a 'closed too early' mechanism: early first contact is a CONSEQUENCE of the lateral drift, not its cause. The 2.45-9.12 cm ejection displacements are the 16 forensic TRAIN tuning closes; v2's GATED failures were 2.70-19.10 cm. The branch exclusion removes the corpus's only dense close-phase coverage (all 597 branches start at the pre-grasp state, BRANCH_PHASE=2). The collector closes on a COUNTER, not an observable event.

declared_risks.R2_shortcut_perception: The encoder's grasp-cohort accuracy is measured on the scripted collector's own stereotyped state distribution. If part of it comes from inferring the apple's position from where the PALM is (known from proprioception anyway) rather than from the apple's pixels, it evaporates off-distribution: right on every frame we can score, wrong on every frame that matters. This is the shape of the last five failures and nothing in the record rules it out. Aggravating: the aim-offset exclusion removes the 20% of the corpus with the MOST apple-position variation relative to the palm.
declared_risks.R3_close_timing: the collector closes on a counter, not an observable event; expect failures at close entry
declared_risks.R4_mean_apple_regression: if vision contributes nothing the policy servos to the corpus-mean apple and behaves like a closed-loop demo_replay; this is exactly what G2 measures
declared_risks.R5_grasp_command_smearing: a regression head on a near-binary target (std 0.865, 34.7% interior) emits interior values; reported as a separate metric, never folded into the action error
declared_risks.R6_single_seed: one training seed per arm; every difference between arms is a single-run difference

evidence_framing.claim: HYPOTHESIS (not a finding): The encoder's PERCEPTION on a nearly-current frame is good, it was never the gated quantity, and it is what a reactive controller needs.
evidence_framing.claim_that_is_NOT_made: The world model works. It does not: no gate in this protocol tests the model's dynamics and none is claimed to.
evidence_framing.decisive_limitation_stated_first: The h~0 perception on the grasp-relevant cohort has NEVER been measured in this project. The claim is a HYPOTHESIS, not a finding, and P1 is its first direct test.
evidence_framing.held_auroc_on_encoded_latents_is_unmeasu: The 0.99949 figure is the h=8 ROLLOUT's AUROC (gates.G5_held_auroc_lift_h8). The AUROC of apple_held on an ENCODED CURRENT latent has never been measured in this project; the pre-flight produces it. The run-time monitor gates nothing.
evidence_framing.not_a_contradiction_of_the_merged_record: This protocol does not dispute README/DECISIONS' 2.35-2.59 cm and does not claim a better encoder number. It claims only that the quantity those figures report -- directly-encoded readout on the MOVING cohort -- is not the quantity a reactive controller depends on, and that the quantity it does depend on is unmeasured.

only_committed_h0_numbers.note: computed in world_model_v4.py L111-115 as ||readout(encode(frame)) - truth||. These are exactly the 2.35-2.59 cm README/DECISIONS publish, and BOTH EXCEED P1's 1.5 cm threshold.

refutation_carried_as_stated_context.reading_of_the_auroc_split: At h=1 the apple_held readout computed from a DIFFERENT window's actions is as good as the real one (0.99737 vs 0.99950). A readout computable from someone else's actions is reading the frame, not the dynamics. The gap opens only as the frame goes stale, which is where the model fails.
refutation_carried_as_stated_context.reading_of_the_ratio: At one step ahead the model's action-conditioned rollout is 5% better than assuming nothing moves. h=8 is gate G2a and is committed; h=1 and h=16 are unverified_pending_P0 item U2.

evidence_framing.the_one_load_bearing_inference: At h=1 the shuffled-action AUROC is 0.99737 against a real-action 0.99950, so the h=1 rollout readout is CLOSE TO what the encoded latent alone supports, and the grasp-cohort h=1 figure of 0.834 cm is the best available hint that close-phase perception beats the moving-cohort 2.35 cm. That is an INFERENCE ACROSS A ONE-STEP PREDICTOR, NOT A MEASUREMENT. The h=8 and h=16 figures are not evidence for the hypothesis at all.
evidence_framing.which_numbers_are_rollouts: world_model_v2.window_metrics computes palm_apple_median_m, palm_apple_grasp_cohort_median_m, G4 and G5 from predicted_readouts(model, arrays, starts, actions, ...) -- see world_model_v2.py L381 'palm = error(predicted, "palm_minus_apple")'. They are h-step ACTION-CONDITIONED ROLLOUT readouts, NOT perception measurements, and this protocol does not present them as such.

gate_threshold_derivation.G1: Null p0 = 0.25 (demo_replay 6/24, verified from committed results documents). One-sided binomial P(X>=17|40,0.25) = 0.0116; Wilson95 [28.5,57.8]. Power 0.866 at a true rate of 0.50, 0.992 at 0.60. Comparison at the same null: 14/40 -> p=0.103, 15/40 -> 0.054, 16/40 -> 0.026. 17/40 = 42.5% is deliberately far below scripted_oracle's 24/24 and far below TASK-034's 16/20 (80%): this gate asks for the FIRST learned success, not the MVP. The second condition prevents a pathological pass on a cohort that happens to be easy for open-loop replay.
gate_threshold_derivation.G2_G3: Exact one-sided McNemar under H0 (equal rates, discordant pairs exchangeable, b ~ Bin(n_d, 0.5), reject when b - c >= 8): p <= 0.0039 at n_d=8, 0.0193 at 12, 0.0384 at 16, 0.0577 at 20, 0.0758 at 24. So p <= 0.05 for any discordance UP TO 16 PAIRS -- stated exactly that precisely, and NOT beyond. +6 was CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: at n_d=12/16/20 it gives 0.073/0.105/0.132. (At n_d=8 and 10 the d>=6 rule is nominally 0.0352 and 0.0547, but those discordance counts cannot arise when G1 requires >=17 successes and A0 is near 0, which forces n_d >= 17.) The realized n_d and exact p are reported alongside the count in every case; the fixed threshold is never re-read as a significance claim beyond the range where it holds.
gate_threshold_derivation.G4: Null p0 = 0.3333 (demo_replay 8/24, verified). One-sided binomial P(X>=20|40,1/3) = 0.0214; Wilson95 [35.2,64.8]. Power 0.926 at a true rate of 0.60. 19/40 -> p=0.044 was considered; 20/40 taken as the round number just above. Grasp is the stage the entire object-ceiling line identified as decisive.
gate_threshold_derivation.G5: measured: hold and random 0/50 on apple->plate; scripted_oracle 24/24 pooled over three prior wide cohorts. A failure here invalidates the RUN, not the arms.
gate_threshold_derivation.G6: non-negotiable project rule (AGENTS.md). Any violation VOIDS the run. The assertion covers A4: its single reset-time truth read is REPLACED, not permitted.
gate_threshold_derivation.G7: the CEM ceiling ran at 0.621-0.649 s per command against a 10 s deadline; a feed-forward policy has no excuse for exceeding 100 ms, and a slow arm would falsify the budget.

gates.G1_also_requires: strictly more than demo_replay's own count on the identical 40 resets

integrity_guard_change.policy_py_excluded_by_design: src/embodied_jepa/policy.py runs INSIDE the control loop -- its inputs become the robot's inputs -- so a label there would be a genuine leak. It imports no label module and must not.
integrity_guard_change.rule_unchanged: Training runners may build targets from labels; control-loop code may not. world_model_v2.py is on the list because it builds readout targets; cloning.py is on it because it reads collector__base_action as the BC target under the same acknowledge_privileged_training_labels gate. This APPLIES the existing rule to a new trainer; it does not relax it.
integrity_guard_change.what: src/embodied_jepa/cloning.py was added to the allow-list of tests/test_apple_wide_collection.py::test_model_planner_and_evaluation_code_never_import_training_labels during stage 2 of this protocol.
integrity_guard_change.which_check_is_load_bearing: Two guards protect policy.py and they are NOT equivalent. 'assert "policy.py" not in allowed' is a tautology against a literal set: it can only fail when someone edits that set, which is exactly and only its job (a future widening fails loudly instead of silently). THE LOAD-BEARING CHECK IS THE LOOP BENEATH IT, which parses every non-allow-listed module and asserts it neither mentions nor imports a label module; policy.py is covered by that loop PRECISELY BECAUSE it is not on the allow-list. Removing the loop on the grounds that the assertion covers it would delete the real protection and leave a tautology behind.
integrity_guard_change.why_recorded_here: A leakage guard was widened during an active protocol by the agent running that protocol. It is defensible, and it was checked independently by the coordinator, but a future auditor comparing the guard before and after TASK-056 deserves to find the reasoning in the record rather than reconstruct it from a diff.

lesson_recorded.a_green_local_suite_is_not_evidence_for_: The first CI run of this preregistration failed on Linux x86-64 while the full suite passed locally on macOS arm64, because a test asserted exact float equality between a stored cohort value and a regenerated one. Locally the generator reproduced the stored values with ZERO deviation, so no amount of local testing could have surfaced it. This protocol's credibility rests on a third party being able to verify the seal on a different machine, so the class of claim matters more than the instance: any assertion that something is bit-identical must be validated on more than one platform, or stated as holding only on the platform that produced it.

pre_declared_outcomes.A_g1_g2_g4_pass: The first learned, non-privileged Apple->Plate successes exist. Next: TASK-034's fresh-cohort validation (new frozen cohort n>=50, >=3 training seeds per arm, full stage breakdown, Wilson intervals, replay video, matched hold/random controls). If G3 also failed, TASK-034 must carry the random-encoder arm forward as a CO-PRIMARY, and no claim that the world model drives the robot is made until G3 passes there. TASK-034's own thresholds are NOT modified by this protocol.
pre_declared_outcomes.B_g4_passes_g1_fails: Grasps but does not place. Perception and approach work; the failure is downstream. This is the v2-object-ceiling profile exactly and has a known, already-passing, non-learned remedy: the v3 release predictor and phase design (24/24). Next: keep the learned approach and grasp, hand transport and place to the v3 phase machine. DO NOT retrain the policy.
pre_declared_outcomes.C_g1_g4_fail_but_A4_succeeds: Perception is adequate in the closed loop and CLONING is the failing component. The binding constraint is the demonstration set. Next task is data collection with a spec: >=500 clean roots, no aim offsets, no corrupted branches, DART noise only, close phase oversampled (risk R1), ~2 h of compute at the committed collection rate (2345.9 s collection + 883.2 s assembly for 797 episodes on 12 workers). Only then is BC retried.
pre_declared_outcomes.D_abandonment_clause: If Outcome D holds, THIS LINE STOPS. No third control formulation is preregistered on this corpus and this camera. The next task is a perception/data task (resolution, camera placement, corpus design), and if that does not move the closed-loop number either, the honest published conclusion is that a 112 px onboard camera plus a single-mode scripted-collector corpus does not support learned Apple->Plate on this platform, and the product goal needs a data or hardware change, not another model.
pre_declared_outcomes.D_g1_g4_fail_and_A4_also_fails: The readouts are accurate on recorded frames and do not survive the state distribution their own controller induces. That is covariate shift, and it is the last five generations' failure in a different costume.
pre_declared_outcomes.D_if_A4_was_dropped: Outcome D still fires and is reported as REACHED ON PARTIAL EVIDENCE, with that stated.
pre_declared_outcomes.D_if_P2_failed: Outcome D still fires and is reported as REACHED ON PARTIAL EVIDENCE, with the P2 value stated, exactly as for a dropped A4. A P2 failure is not an escape from the abandonment clause.
pre_declared_outcomes.E_p1_fails: The task stops before training, IN EVERY SUB-CASE. See preflight.P1_abort_rule. Takes precedence over every other outcome. The sub-cases exist ONLY to make the abort produce a usable next task instead of a bare stop; they change nothing about whether this task proceeds, and NO sub-case permits continuing. There is no value of P1 above the threshold for which any arm is trained, any feature is precomputed for training, or any cohort is opened.

E_sub_cases_affect_only_the_next_task.E_clear: The ratio passed AND P1 >= 2.0 cm. A CLEAR FAILURE: not distinguishable from the blind prior in any way that matters. Begin with the demoted v3 information-ceiling probe (single-frame apple-position regression at 112 px and at the native render resolution, no dynamics).
E_sub_cases_affect_only_the_next_task.E_near: The ratio passed AND P1 in [1.5, 2.0) cm. A NEAR MISS, recorded as a distinct reading: perception is materially better than the 2.394 cm no-vision prior but not inside the grasp boundary the task turns on. Follow-up is a perception/data task with a concrete target: render resolution, camera placement, close-phase coverage (risk R1).
E_sub_cases_affect_only_the_next_task.E_prior: P1's RATIO to the P0a control failed, whatever its absolute value. The encoder is reading the prior, not the apple. TAKES PRECEDENCE over E_near and E_clear, because a small absolute value here is not evidence of good perception. No amount of resolution fixes it, so the follow-up is the information-ceiling probe, NEVER a resolution change.
E_sub_cases_affect_only_the_next_task.agent_does_not_choose: In every sub-case the executing agent stops and reports to the coordinator and does not select the follow-up itself.
E_sub_cases_affect_only_the_next_task.binding_note: The distinction can only ever affect what the NEXT task is, never whether this one proceeds.
E_sub_cases_affect_only_the_next_task.control_reported_either_way: The P0a shuffled-frame control value is reported alongside P1 whatever happens. '1.7 cm at 0.4x the shuffled control' and '1.7 cm at 0.95x the shuffled control' are very different results and only the first is worth a follow-up: the second says the encoder is reading the prior, not the apple, and no amount of resolution fixes that. The ratio is part of the recorded outcome, not a diagnostic footnote.
E_sub_cases_affect_only_the_next_task.precedence_within_E: E_prior takes precedence over E_near and E_clear. A ratio-only failure must never be labelled E_near just because its absolute value is small: that would point the next generation at resolution when the problem is that the encoder is not reading the apple at all.

pre_declared_outcomes.in_every_outcome: all arms' numbers and all four references are published whatever they say; failures and negative results stay in the results doc and this manifest; the apple-wide-v1 test split is never decoded; cohort C is consumed by this task and never reused; nothing is retuned and re-reported after the gates are read, and any rerun is a new disclosed protocol version.
pre_declared_outcomes.precedence: Outcome E takes precedence over all others; Outcome A takes precedence over B. Preconditions on C and D read 'P1 passed (P2 and P3 recorded whatever they say)': only P1 can stop the task, only P3 can drop an arm, and P2 can neither.

pre_run_review.rule: A gated run starts only on the pre-run reviewer's REPORTED verdict, delivered as a message, never on a review file read from disk. The same rule applies to merging.
three_separate_authorizations: 1. merge the preregistration, on the reviewer's REPORTED APPROVE
2. start the gated run, whose first step is the pre-flight
3. open frozen cohort C, after the pre-flight values, training reports and development numbers have been reported
pre_run_review.why: grasp-closure v3 broke it: the author read an interim 'CLEAR TO RUN' file from the working tree while the reviewer's final verdict was BLOCK

predecessor.clause_this_protocol_implements: behaviour cloning with the world model as a critic or residual becomes the primary line and CEM over this cost is abandoned
predecessor.critic_deliberately_not_implemented: A critic is Q(s,a), a counterfactual action-conditioned value. Every action-conditioned quantity in this model has failed its gate (G2a never passed in any generation; G9 failed on all four v4 arms; held_lift_shuffled_auroc is 0.99737 at h=1, i.e. at short horizon the action is nearly irrelevant to the model's own readout). Building a critic on this model re-imports the failed component under a new name. The critic is a declared follow-up conditioned on Outcome A.
predecessor.overall: All four arms failed the primary gate G2a (0.8763/0.8814/0.8635/0.9036 vs <=0.8) and the untouched control E0 passed more gates (10/14) than every intervention (9/14). Outcome B fired: CEM over this cost is abandoned and behaviour cloning with the world model as a critic or residual becomes the primary line.

preflight.P0a_residual_weakness: Pairing is by phase index alone and orient runs 130 commands, so a foreign frame from early orient can be paired with late-orient proprioception. The encoder then sees an off-distribution combination and may read worse than a fair control would, which INFLATES P0a and makes the ratio EASIER to pass. P0a is a reliable detector of a fully blind or shortcut readout and a somewhat lenient grader of degree. It cannot create a false failure. The runner asserts that at least 95% of frames were re-paired with a foreign image, so a degenerate control is tamper-evident.

P1_abort_rule.agent_stops_and_reports: on a P1 failure the executing agent stops and reports to the coordinator; it does not select a replacement plan on its own
P1_abort_rule.honest_limit: P1 failing does not strictly prove BC impossible, since BC need not route through the readout. It does mean the one demonstrated capability this line rests on is absent. Immediate follow-up: the demoted v3 information-ceiling probe (single-frame apple-position regression at 112 px and at native render resolution, no dynamics).
P1_abort_rule.on_failure: the task STOPS; the per-phase localization table is written to the results doc and the manifest; the outcome is Outcome E; the runner exits non-zero
P1_abort_rule.proceed_anyway_is_not_an_available_outco: there is no branch in pre_declared_outcomes for 'P1 failed but we proceeded because X'

preflight.P1_stays_at_1_5_cm: Coordinator ruling after the review tightened P1's siblings: P1 is CARRIED from G1 rather than invented, and the grasp/eject evidence (holds 0.49-1.35 cm; the lowest gated v2 crossing at 1.61 cm) puts it at the boundary the task actually turns on. Loosening it immediately after its siblings were tightened would be the worst possible time to move it. The near-miss band is the concession, and it affects only the follow-up.

P2_has_a_declared_consequence.loophole_this_closes: Outcomes C and D both read 'P1/P2/P3 passed'; P3 was patched by the dropped-A4 clause and P2 was NOT, so a P2 failure followed by G1 and G4 failing would have matched NO pre-declared outcome and 'Outcome D's preconditions were not met' would have been available as an argument against the abandonment clause.
P2_has_a_declared_consequence.preconditions_now_read: P1 passed (P2 and P3 recorded whatever they say). Only P1 can stop the task; only P3 can drop an arm.
P2_has_a_declared_consequence.rule: A P2 failure changes nothing about which outcome fires. It drops no arm and blocks no gate. It is recorded in pre_run_changes with its value, the runner prints it explicitly, and Outcome D if reached is reported ON PARTIAL EVIDENCE, as for a dropped A4.

preflight.P2_is_expected_to_fail_and_that_is_a_mea: On the moving-cohort reasoning in P3_is_the_threshold_most_likely_to_bite, a P2 failure is EXPECTED rather than surprising. P2 binds nothing (it drops no arm and blocks no gate) and this is declared in advance, so P2 is a RECORDED MEASUREMENT, not a failed gate. REPORTING RULE: the results document and every summary count must report P2 as a measurement with its value and its control ratio, and must NEVER include it in a count of failed gates, or the outcome will read as worse than it is.

P3_is_a_hard_precondition_for_A4.consequence_for_outcome_D: without A4, a joint failure of G1 and G4 can no longer distinguish 'perception is inadequate in the loop' from 'cloning is the failing component'. The abandonment clause STILL FIRES, but is reported as reached ON PARTIAL EVIDENCE and explicitly labelled a weaker reading.
P3_is_a_hard_precondition_for_A4.recorded_as: a pre-run protocol change with its reason and its P3 value, in the results doc and in pre_run_changes; never a silent omission
P3_is_a_hard_precondition_for_A4.rule: if P3 fails, A4 DOES NOT RUN

preflight.P3_is_the_threshold_most_likely_to_bite: Declared before the run. The moving cohort is windows whose palm-apple offset moves >= 1 cm over 8 steps. With translation_per_step_m = 0.015 and the collector's +-0.4 clip a servoing palm covers up to 0.6 cm per step, i.e. up to 4.8 cm over 8, so during orient and descend essentially every frame is a moving window while close and lift hold station. The moving cohort is therefore approximately the APPROACH phases, and E0's one committed h=0 measurement of that population is 2.3536 cm. P2 and P3 are scored on exactly those phases. Consequences are asymmetric: a P2 failure costs nothing and is EXPECTED on this reasoning; a P3 failure drops A4, makes Outcome C unreachable and downgrades Outcome D to partial evidence before the run starts, losing the decomposition A4 exists to provide.
preflight.is_inside_the_gated_run: The pre-flight is part of the gated run, NOT a preliminary. It runs after this preregistration and its manifest have merged, and only once the gated run has been authorized on the pre-run reviewer's reported verdict. It is not a scouting measurement taken before the protocol is sealed, and no closed-loop gate threshold may be adjusted in response to it.
preflight.measurement: frozen E0 readouts on DIRECTLY ENCODED val frames of the 15 surviving val roots, broken out by collector__phase_index

no_vision_control.P0a_shuffled_frame: identical readouts with the IMAGE drawn from a different val episode at the same collector phase, proprioception held. The direct analogue of held_lift_shuffled_auroc. Every gate must beat it by the ratio factor; a MISSING control counts as FAILED, never as a free pass.
no_vision_control.P0b_derivation: wide_reset jitters object_xy by uniform(+-0.03) per axis, so a predictor that always emits the reset centre has median error = median norm of a uniform square = 2.3937 cm (2e6 samples; closed form asserted by the runner).
no_vision_control.what_it_fixed: As originally written P3 (3.0 cm) sat 0.6 cm ABOVE the blind baseline and P2 (2.5 cm) 0.1 cm above it: both were passable by a model that never opens its eyes. Worse, risk R2's declared early-signal ('~1 cm on close but ~4 cm on orient/descend') could not fire, because a pure-prior model reads ~2.4 cm on orient/descend and would have PASSED a 2.5 cm P2.
no_vision_control.why: The protocol's own argument one level up is 'a readout you can compute equally well from someone else's ACTIONS is reading the frame, not the dynamics'. The same argument one level down: a readout you can compute equally well from someone else's FRAME is reading the prior, not the frame.
no_vision_control.why_P1_needs_it_too: scripted.py targets obj + [-0.03, 0, 0.052] in BOTH descend and close, so the collector P-servos the palm to a fixed apple-relative offset and the true palm_minus_apple on close frames is nearly a phase-conditional constant. With state_fusion: true the latent carries the proprioception needed to infer the phase, so a head that has learned that constant scores well on P1 WITHOUT reading the apple's pixels.

preflight.script: scripts/measure_policy_preflight.py (committed as part of this task)

thresholds.P1: 1.5 cm is CARRIED from v3/v4's own G1 threshold, not invented. Corroborated (not derived) by the grasp/eject boundary: grasp-closure v3's 24 ceiling holds sat at close-phase apple xy 0.49-1.35 cm. CORRECTED MARGIN: that document's 'Corrected by this verification' section (L375-386) retracts the 2.45-9.28 cm ejection range for the GATED failures (those were 2.70-19.10 cm; 2.45-9.12 cm are the 16 forensic TRAIN tuning closes) and records that SIX of v2's 16 gated closes crossed the 1.5 cm measure, the lowest at 1.61 cm. The gap around P1 is therefore 1.35 -> 1.61 cm, not 1.35 -> 2.45 cm. Construct note: close_phase_apple_xy_cm measures how far the apple MOVED, not the model's ESTIMATION error; the bridge is stated, not assumed.
thresholds.P2: TIGHTENED from 2.5 cm, which sat 0.1 cm above the 2.394 cm no-vision prior and was therefore passable by a model that never reads the image. 1.5 cm is 0.63x that prior.
thresholds.P3: TIGHTENED from 3.0 cm, which a constant-centre predictor passes outright (2.394 cm) and which therefore certified nothing. 2.0 cm clears the blind prior by 0.4 cm AND stays inside the corpus's own 1.5-3.0 cm injected mis-aim band, which is the band A4 must live in. An intermediate draft set it to 1.5 cm to 'match P1's scale'; that was aesthetic and would very likely have PRE-DOOMED A4.
thresholds.ratio: 0.7 is A JUDGEMENT CALL FIXED IN ADVANCE, not a derivation. What makes it acceptable is that P0a has never been measured, so 0.7 cannot have been reverse-engineered from a known value; the realized ratio is reported whatever it turns out to be. It mirrors the repo's G2a idiom (error / a baseline) and is stricter than G2a's 0.8 because this baseline carries zero information.

preflight.what_P1_certifies: P1 measures readout(encode(image, robot_state)), which for E0 (state_fusion: true) fuses proprioception -- that is exactly A4's front end. A2 instead consumes image_features (image-only) plus separately-normalized proprioception through a learned head. A P1 pass is therefore DIRECT evidence for A4's pathway and only INDIRECT evidence for A2's.
preflight.what_makes_P3_at_2_0_cm_safe: Not the 0.39 cm gap to the blind prior, which is thin. The ratio condition: a blind or shortcut readout scores the same with a foreign frame as with its own, so its ratio is ~1.0 and it fails <= 0.7 decisively. The absolute threshold keeps the gate inside the corpus's own 1.5-3.0 cm mis-aim band that A4 must live in; the ratio keeps it honest.

best_ever_g2a.note: 0.8635 is only the best IN V4 (arm E2). docs/DECISIONS.md: 'G2a has never passed: 0.835 at v2, 0.831 at best in v3.' Against a threshold of 0.8 the whole line's best attempt missed by 4%.

frozen_wall_clock_caps_differ_by_generat.note: 10800 s is not a standing limit; each protocol freezes its own budget

rebased_onto.models_md_note: docs/MODELS.md records that state_fusion and readout_heads have NOT been ablated on/off: untested rather than shown to help. This protocol depends on state_fusion being ON in E0 (arms use image_features, not encode(), so the A0 ablation stays honest) and says so.

observations.A0_is_now_the_most_informative_arm: If relative palm-apple accuracy is largely recoverable from proprioception, a proprioception-only policy may be strong, and G2 (best learned arm - A0) becomes the gate that decides whether anything visual is happening at all. A0 is to be built and trained with the same care as A2. If A0 turns out strong, that is a FINDING, not an inconvenience.
observations.P2_ratio_margin: 0.682 against the 0.7 threshold, a margin of 0.018. PASSES. No threshold was adjusted in response. On approach frames a FOREIGN image still yields 0.669 cm, so most of the RELATIVE palm-apple accuracy is available without looking at the apple: the R2 shortcut signature partially present. At the first draft's P2 of 2.5 cm with no control this would have been invisible.
observations.P3_is_the_cleanest_measurement: Its control lands at 2.269 cm, essentially on the 2.394 cm analytic blind prior: absolute apple position genuinely cannot be inferred from the palm's own pose, so P3 is the one measurement here with NO shortcut available to it. The model reads 0.873 cm against it. This is the result that most supports A4.
observations.R2_not_borne_out_as_written: R2 was that the encoder might localize the apple only once the palm is beside it. Approach phases read 0.404-0.490 cm, so the accuracy is not confined to the close phase.
observations.place_phase_flagged_in_advance: release_high 1.579 cm and lower_open 4.084 cm are far worse than every other phase (the apple is at the plate, partly out of the onboard view). A4's place phase runs exactly there and the v3 release predictor has no learned substitute. RECORDED BEFORE ANY ARM RUNS: if A4 grasps reliably and then fails at the plate, that is the failure this table predicted.

stage1_withdrawal_clause.committed: 2026-09-24, while the alignment review of the runner was still running and its answer was unknown.
stage1_withdrawal_clause.expectation: Not expected to fire. If it does not, the clause stays in the record as what was committed to while the answer was still open.
if_a_defect_is_found: STOP AND REPORT BEFORE FIXING ANYTHING. Added as a refinement that makes this clause STRICTER: the original wording went straight to 'the fix lands', which would have permitted a repair as a reflex inside a merge. A defect here has implications wider than one script, so the response is decided deliberately with the coordinator rather than chosen by whoever finds it.
The stage-1 result is WITHDRAWN, not patched: section 1's gate table stops being the result.
The fix lands and the runner RE-RUNS from the same frozen checkpoint; the new numbers stand on their own, INCLUDING the possibility that a gate which passed now fails and Outcome E fires.
The 0.491 / 0.456 / 0.873 figures are NOT carried forward alongside a corrected runner; they are reported as withdrawn, next to what replaced them.
NO argument is entertained about whether the defect 'would have mattered'. A result whose correctness was established by reasoning after the fact is not a measurement.
The withdrawal, the defect and the re-run are recorded with BOTH sets of numbers, so the record shows what we believed and what corrected it.
stage1_withdrawal_clause.related_exposure_named_not_acted_on: The same gap -- verifying a number's VALUE does not verify WHAT PRODUCED IT -- applies in principle to every accepted numerical claim in the experiment record, and the claims nobody has had reason to re-examine carry it most, since 'nobody re-examined it' is not evidence of anything. Re-auditing the record from inside a running experiment is how a protocol stops being a protocol, so it is NOT done here and NO task is opened for it by this protocol. Recorded so it is carried rather than forgotten.
stage1_withdrawal_clause.the_unverified_dependency: shuffled_frame_control deliberately uses TWO DIFFERENT row arrays (image_rows for the image, rows for the proprioception) and compares the readouts against truth[valid_rows]. The stage-1 result was accepted on its VALUES; the row/position correspondence underneath them was not checked. Same shape of gap as the rollout-versus-perception error that section 1 was rewritten to fix.
stage1_withdrawal_clause.why_now: Cheap to commit to in advance, expensive to argue about once a passing result is in hand and a day of work sits behind it.

training.declared_selection_weakness: val action error is a WEAK proxy for closed-loop success. It is used because selecting on closed-loop outcomes would either consume the frozen cohort or select on the gate metric. Stated in advance.
training.selection_metric: median per-dimension expert action error on masked val frames of the 15 surviving val roots
training.selection_metric_as_implemented: The frozen wording is 'median per-dimension expert action error'. cloning.action_error computes np.median over the flattened [N,7] error array, which is the median over all dimensions jointly, NOT the median of the seven per-dimension medians. The per-dimension medians ARE recorded alongside it in every validation event, so either reading is recoverable from the artifact. Disclosed rather than changed: the frozen text is not edited after the fact.

what_a_pass_would_and_would_not_mean: G1 passing would be the first learned, non-privileged Apple->Plate success in this project. It would NOT be an MVP: 17/40 = 42.5% against TASK-034's 16/20 = 80%.
G1 is not passable by any control in this protocol: hold and random are 0/50 measured, demo_replay is 6/24, A0 and A1 are gated against separately.

G1 passing while G2 fails would mean almost nothing and is read that way: it would say the policy reproduces the schedule on a cohort the schedule happens to fit. G1 and G2 are read jointly, never G1 alone.
G4 can pass while G1 fails (grasps that do not place). That is Outcome B and it has a known non-learned remedy.
NO gate in this protocol tests the world model's dynamics, and none is claimed to.
A4 succeeding is not a learned-policy result and is never reported as one.
n=40 with ONE training seed per arm. Every difference between arms is a single-run difference, as in v3 and v4. Multiple seeds are TASK-034's job.
